decision: Keep sites excluded when researchers or ecological criteria call for it. Do not choose sites by the results.
why: Researcher advice and ecological fit determine site eligibility, not whether a result is large or statistically clear.
full_rule: Preserve researcher and ecological exclusions. Do not select sites by slope, significance or effect direction.

decision: Use at least three matched, usable years before designation and three usable years after. Count the designation year as after. Keep all supported years, with no nine-year limit. Check four before years and a continuing pre-protection trend as alternatives.
why: The same time rule should apply to every comparison. The alternative fits show how much the baseline choice matters.
full_rule: Three matched strictly earlier calendar years; designation year after. At least three observed post years; all supported observed years, no nine-year cap or consecutive-year requirement. Four-before-year sensitivity. Flat-baseline level/recovery model with pre-trend sensitivity; otherwise post-protection trend only.
status: Frozen for integrated review; no result-direction selection

decision: Compare protected and reference surveys only where they share recorded depth zones. Also check results using the same zones throughout.
why: A depth difference can look like a biological change. A shared zone name helps, but it does not guarantee the same depth or habitat.
applies_to: Integrated diver comparisons with recorded comparable zones; physical-depth limitations retained
full_rule: Use shared program depth zones within each comparison/year; constant-zone sensitivity. Do not equate a shared label with demonstrated physical-depth or habitat equivalence.
status: Integrated review and fitted coverage sensitivities
limitation: Shared recorded zones do not establish physical-depth or habitat equivalence; earlier six-history zone counts are historical.

decision: Keep valid surveys from any month. Give repeat visits equal weight within zones, then average zones within stations and stations within each side.
why: There is no supported reason to discard all surveys outside one season. Repeated visits should not count as extra stations.
applies_to: Integrated diver survey records; program-specific nested unit weights
full_rule: Retain valid survey dates in all months; equal dated visits within zones, equal zones within stations and available documented stations within roles.
limitation: Replaces May–October restriction for this review only; seasonal imbalance remains

decision: Keep the 2004 CRANE fish surveys and average repeat surveys. Leave out incomplete passes when calculating the combined fish measure.
why: A missing fish survey level is not a count of zero. The available CRANE records follow the approved survey rule.
full_rule: Retain CRANE, average repeat surveys and omit incomplete passes from the combined fish response.
limitation: Do not treat missing levels as zero counts

decision: Use the documented stations surveyed each year. Check whether results change when the station set stays constant.
why: A changing set of stations could change the apparent trend.
full_rule: Use available documented stations each year; preserve response-specific exclusions. Constant-station sensitivity and explicit shared-reference models.
status: Integrated review and fitted coverage sensitivities

decision: Treat missing counts and sizes as missing. Keep a density result when counts are sound but biomass is not.
why: Missing size data should not erase a valid count history.
full_rule: Unknown counts and positive-count missing sizes remain unknown; preserve density independently. Same-site/date mean-mass lobster imputation retains shared donors.
limitation: Unknown records remain unknown. Source reconstruction and recovery review completed; downstream paper analyses still require regeneration.

decision: Keep excluded sites out, even if their names or group labels differ across files.
why: Different names for the same excluded site must not bring its measurements back into the analysis.
applies_to: All documented response-specific exclusions, including count, donor and calibration records
full_rule: Apply exclusions by verified physical site to counts, size donors and calibration; keep KFM benthic exclusions distinct from fish exclusions.
status: Corrected source build completed in isolated folder

decision: Use sizes from the counted site and survey when possible. For KFM, allow sizes measured within seven days; use the separate tested borrowing rule for PISCO.
why: Sizes from other places or distant dates may not represent the animals counted.
applies_to: Integrated size-based biomass; KFM urchin/kelp short-gap rule and restricted PISCO calibrated borrowing
full_rule: Use sizes from the count visit first. KFM urchin/kelp: nearest same-site/year sizes within seven days; exact-date sensitivity. Allow calibrated PISCO reference borrowing only within the six reviewed histories and declared donor rules. Keep density where biomass lacks size support.
status: Integrated donor ledger and direct-size-only refit; unsupported biomass stays missing
limitation: Supersedes unrestricted nearest-date matching in earlier local-only review

decision: Borrow sizes only from reviewed reference surveys of the same species, protected area, zone and year. Test each borrowing rule without using the target site to calibrate itself.
why: Borrowed sizes can alter biomass; donors should be comparable to the count survey.
full_rule: For the six reviewed PISCO animal-biomass histories, borrow reference sizes only within the same species, MPA, reference role, zone and calendar year. Exclude the target site from cross-site donors and calibration.
status: Incorporated into integrated biomass within the six-history target/calibration scope
limitation: Only reference-side borrowing has been evaluated. Matching zone and year does not prove comparable animal sizes; calibration residuals pool zones and years within each response history and role.

decision: For PISCO borrowing, allow no larger count–size date gap than the one tested for that comparison. Require at least two calibration site-years.
why: A larger date gap would go beyond what the data used to test borrowing can support. Two calibration site-years remain sparse evidence.
full_rule: For reviewed PISCO borrowing, require the donor–count date gap to be no larger than the largest gap observed in that comparison’s calibration data, with zero extra days of tolerance and at least two calibration site-year groups. This is not proof of strong validation.
limitation: Two calibration groups is a computational minimum, not strong validation. No extra PISCO tolerance beyond the strict calibration maximum is adopted; the KFM seven-day rule is separate.

decision: Require biomass support for every retained station and visit in a comparison-year. Do not drop a station only to make biomass calculable.
why: Dropping unsupported stations only for biomass would change the site comparison.
applies_to: All integrated biomass role-years; density assessed independently
full_rule: Require support for every retained surveyed station/visit in each role-year. Do not remove an unsupported station to rescue biomass; density is separate.
status: Integrated yearly support and eligibility tables
limitation: Earlier 44/63 totals apply only to the six-series borrowing audit; use the integrated annual roster for current coverage.

decision: Account for repeated use of counts, sizes and reference sites, and for change through time. State what the available data cannot measure.
why: Shared measurements and reference sites make estimates less independent than they first appear.
applies_to: All integrated response histories; shared measurement and process uncertainty
full_rule: Shared physical count units, frequency-aware size draws, imputation donors and calibration errors feed joint calendar-AR models with shared-reference process terms. Report unestimable uncertainty separately.
status: Integrated conditional uncertainty; boundary and sensitivity diagnostics retained
limitation: Intervals are conditional on recorded sizes and fixed conversion equations. LTER within-group size variation, allometric coefficient covariance, detection and missing habitat information remain unmeasured. The 20% and 30% group-size scenarios are assumptions, not confidence bounds.

decision: Review these results before changing the paper. Then rerun the linked analyses and check every reported result.
why: The paper should report one checked set of analyses and results.
full_rule: Review cohort and models are frozen in configuration; paper adoption remains on hold pending review and downstream pathway/resilience/figure regeneration.
status: Integrated review completed; no paper promotion
limitation: Review configuration frozen; final paper release not approved or certified.

decision: Set borrowing rules before looking at the effects. Show which biomass results depend on borrowed sizes and what happens with direct sizes only.
why: The direct-size-only check shows how much the biomass result relies on borrowing.
applies_to: Current integrated biomass review; six calibrated PISCO borrowing histories
full_rule: Choose direct-size and borrowing eligibility before examining effects. Report the supported biomass years and direct-size-only sensitivity alongside any result that uses borrowed sizes; preserve density when biomass is unsupported.
status: Coverage and direct-size-only joint refit completed for review
limitation: Borrowing supports 20 PISCO comparison-years. Removing it changes fitted coverage; retained annual values and measurement draws do not change. This does not establish donor representativeness.
